  NEW BUSINESS
  ~ GENERAL PLAN AMEMDMENT - DOWNTOWN SPECIFIC PLAN
  (PGPA1901560), &
  ~  ZONING CODE TEXT AMENDMENT (PZC1901561)
  LOCATION:  CITYWIDE
  APPLICANT:  CITY OF GLENDALE
  STAFF:  Bradley Calvert, Assistant Director, and Vilia Zemaitaitis, Principal
  Planner

  PROJECT DESCRIPTION
  It is proposed to comprehensively amend the Downtown Specific Plan (DSP),
  generally relating to Urban Design, Open Space and Community Benefits, as well as
  minor changes and clarifications, and Chapter 30.32 of the Glendale Municipal Code,
  1995, relating to the hotel parking requirement.

  ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION
  An addendum to the previously certified Environmental Impact Report for the
  Downtown Specific Plan (DSP EIR) was prepared for the amendments.

  STAFF
  Staff Members Bradley Calvert and Vilia Zemaitaitis presented a powerpoint
  presentation highlighting the main points in the Planning Commission staff report
  and the proposed DSP Amendments.

  Ms. Zemaitaitis described the history of the DSP amendments and informed the
  Planning Commissioners that City Council adopted a moratorium last year regarding
  residential development in the Downtown. Council also unanimously voted to initiate
  the process of amending the Downtown Specific Plan (DSP) with respect to
  standards, height, and F.A.R. incentives, and additional miscellaneous standards.
  The current DSP amendments take into account City Council's vision for the DSP,
  following a series of meetings and workshops with Council. The DSP amendments
  are primarily an urban design-oriented set of updates that focuses on standards to
  improve streetscapes and the pedestrian experience, public accessible open space
  areas, building facades, and overall building massing.

  The bulk of the proposed DSP amendments are in Chapter 4 - Urban Design,
  Chapter 5 - Open Space and Chapter 7 - Community Benefits. Bradley Calvert

  2
 Special Planning Commission Minutes
February 19, 2019

  highlighted the amendments regarding Urban Design. Vilia Zemaitaitis then
  proceeded with updates to the Public Realm and Open Space, followed by changes
  to the previous Chapter 7 - Incentives and Bonuses. Bradley Calvert described the
  new tiered Community Benefit program in Chapter 7. Staff then highlighted several
  minor items modified in the draft DSP following Planning Commission staff report
  distribution, and that public outreach was or will be made to the following groups:
  Design Review Board, Chamber of Commerce, Royal Canyon Property Owners
  Association, Northwest Glendale Homeowners' Association , Glendale Homeowner's
  Coordinating Council , and Downtown Glendale Association.

  Staff member Vilia Zemaitaitis concluded that Community Development
  Department staff recommends that the Planning Commission consider the
  proposed amendments to the Downtown Specific Plan and zoning text regarding
  the hotel parking requirement, and recommend approval to the City Council, as
  stated in the staff report dated February 19, 2019.

  WRITTEN COMMUNICATION
  In Support:  None.
  Interested Persons: None
  In Opposition
  - N. Soghbatyan (submitted email)

  SPEAKING AT THE HEARING
  In Support:  No one.
  In Opposition:  No one.
  Interested Persons: No one.

  DISCUSSION BY COMMISSIONERS
  Upon questioning by the Planning Commissioners, Ms. Zemaitaitis stated that:
  Building & Safety and Public Works no longer allow overhangs or balconies
  over the public right-of-way.
  City Council is the Design Review authority for projects in the DSP, not the Design
  Review Board .

  Planning Commissioners discussed the following:
  Council 's number of units per acre versus FAR presentation on February 12th
  Open space and the dimensional criteria standard mentioned by ORB
  Diversity of housing standards
  Density bonus projects in the DSP and how incentives and waivers would be
  addressed in the Community Benefits program
  Overhang balconies and other projections no longer permitted in DSP over
  sidewalks
  Mobility Plan - Traffic Plan to be addressed and Circulation Element should be
  updated
  Attraction of small-scale businesses along connector streets and gap analysis
  should be conducted

  3
 Special Planning Commission Minutes
February 19, 2019

  Whether projects in the downtown area should be reviewed by the Design
  Review Board for recommendation prior to Council
  Whether a minimum number of 2- and 3-bedroom units should be required in
  by-right projects
  Tiered Community Benefit System in DSP and raising percentages of Diversity
  of Housing in Tiers II and Ill
  Feedback from the Chamber of Commerce and Homeowners' Associations

  MOTION
  GENERAL PLAN AMEMDMENT- DOWNTOWN SPECIFIC PLAN (PGPA1901560)
 Moved by Planning Commissioner Astorian, and seconded by Planning Commissioner
 Chraghchian, that after review and consideration of an Addendum to the Final
 Environmental Impact Report for the Downtown Specific Plan pursuant to the California
 Environmental Quality Act, and proposed Downtown Specific Plan amendments generally
 relating to urban design , open space, community benefits, as well as other miscellaneous
 texts amendments (PGPA 1901560), and after a duly-noticed public hearing of the
 Planning Commission, the Planning Commission hereby recommends that the City
 Council adopt the proposed amendments to the Downtown Specific Plan, subject to the
 recommendation made by the Planning Commissioners at the hearing to increase the
 minimum diversity in housing mix (the number of 2- and 3-bedroom units) percentages
 from 20% to 25% for Tier 11 projects and from 30% to 35% for Tier 111 projects utilizing the
 Tiered Community Benefit System in the Downtown Specific Plan Chapter 7 - Community
 Benefits, in order to better ensure a range of housing opportunities.
 Adopted this 19th day of February, 2019.

 VOTE
 Ayes:  Astorian, Chraghchian, Lee, Shahbazian
 Noes:  None
 Absent:  None
 Abstain:  None

  MOTION
  ZONING CODE TEXT AMENDMENT (PZC1901561)
Moved by Planning Commissioner Lee, and seconded by Planning Commissioner
Astorian, that after review and consideration of an Addendum to the Final Environmental
Impact Report for the Downtown Specific Plan pursuant to the California Environmental
Quality Act and proposed zoning code text amendment to Section 30.32.050, generally
relating to hotel parking requirement (Case No. PZC 1901561 ), and after a duly-noticed
public hearing of the Planning Commission , the Planning Commission hereby
recommends that the City Council adopt the proposed amendment to Title 30 of the
Glendale Municipal Code, 1995.
Adopted this 19th day of February, 2019.
